stories.what: The ZEUS trial, shown at the American Heart Association meeting, found the inflammation-blocking antibody ziltivekimab lowered inflammation markers but did not reduce heart attacks, strokes or cardiovascular death (17.6% vs 17.7%) in people with heart disease and kidney disease.
stories.why: A test of whether blocking inflammation alone protects the heart came back negative in a very high-risk group; bears directly on that record. Topline was announced 2026-07-31; full data now.

stories.what: The FDA approved Bayer's Sunharbo (asundexian), a once-daily factor XIa blocker, with antiplatelet medicine to lower the risk of a repeat stroke after a recent mild-to-moderate stroke or high-risk mini-stroke. In a large phase 3 trial it cut ischemic stroke by 26% against placebo, with more major bleeding in people over 75 and in the first 90 days.
stories.why: First approval of a new class of clot-preventing drug for age-related stroke; adjacent to the age-disease approvals the site follows, but not an ageing treatment itself. Match to the record is loose (approval of a cardiovascular-prevention drug).

stories.what: A paper reports that six blood-protein age clocks all read the treated group as biologically younger in a 12-week phase 2a trial of rentosertib, a drug for lung scarring. The clocks cannot separate an effect on ageing from an effect on the disease.
stories.why: A controlled-trial drug moved age clocks, though in a disease population; caveat limits it.

stories.what: At the ageing-research meeting ARDD in Boston, senior FDA leaders called longevity a priority and discussed fit-for-purpose endpoints and clearer pathways for treatments aimed at ageing biology. Life Biosciences separately reported interim data (first released 2026-10-08) for ER-100, a partial-reprogramming eye gene therapy, in three glaucoma patients.
stories.why: Regulator signals only, no formal recognition; the reprogramming data is older than the window.

stories.what: Acumen's phase 2 trial of sabirnetug in early Alzheimer disease did not meet its main goal at 18 months, though amyloid scans showed less plaque. Acumen is ending development of the drug.
stories.why: Another amyloid antibody that cleared plaque without a clinical benefit. Topline was first announced 2026-10-30; page dated 11-03.

stories.what: The full Lp(a)HORIZON results were presented at the American Heart Association meeting and published in the New England Journal of Medicine: pelacarsen cut lipoprotein(a) sharply in 8,323 patients but did not reduce heart events (death 5.7% vs 5.9%). Topline had been announced in September.
stories.why: Large negative heart-prevention trial; Novartis ended the programme.

stories.what: A six-month placebo-controlled University of Surrey trial of the supplement NOVOS Core in 61 healthy adults around 60 found better blood-vessel function and lower arterial stiffness and systolic blood pressure (6.1 mmHg). Dropout was high and the maker helped fund it.

Muna Therapeutics reported phase 1 results for MNA-001, an oral pill that activates TREM2 in brain immune cells; in elderly volunteers some age-linked markers in spinal fluid moved toward younger levels. No cognitive benefit shown; phase 2 planned for early 2027.

Novartis ended its option and license deal with BioArctic for a brain-delivery technology, leaving BioArctic with the $30 million upfront payment and no milestones. The technology has not yet been tested in humans.
stories.why: Deal setback in Alzheimer's drug delivery.

stories.what: The FDA issued final guidance on checking the strength (potency) of each batch of cell and gene therapies, replacing its 2011 guidance.
stories.why: Lowers a manufacturing hurdle for cell and gene therapies, including reprogramming.

stories.what: Eisai announced it will present five-year Clarity AD follow-up results for lecanemab at the CTAD meeting in Boston on November 16. No outcome data were released.
stories.why: Preview of a result due after the window.

stories.what: A new registered trial (Phase 1/2, Steadman Philippon Research Institute) will evaluate the supplement fisetin to reduce body-wide ageing (senescent) cells. A second registration tests faecal microbiota transplants to slow biological ageing.
stories.why: Registry listing seen via API (first posted 2026-11-05); page itself did not render, so not opened.
